candidate.blueprint_topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — ABI interpretation for PAD
candidate.educational_objective: Interpret an abnormal resting ankle-brachial index in a client evaluated for peripheral artery disease.

options.A: It is within the normal ABI range and supports normal lower-extremity arterial perfusion
options.B: It primarily indicates impaired venous return rather than arterial disease
options.C: It is abnormal and supports reduced lower-extremity arterial perfusion consistent with peripheral artery disease
options.D: It indicates increased arterial perfusion because ankle pressure is lower than arm pressure

candidate.rationale: The American Heart Association identifies a resting ABI of 1.00 to 1.40 as normal and a value of 0.90 or lower as abnormal. In a client being evaluated for PAD, an ABI of 0.82 therefore supports reduced lower-extremity arterial perfusion and is consistent with PAD. C is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Resting ABI is a standard PAD test; ABI ≤0.90 is abnormal and indicates reduced lower-extremity arterial perfusion in the appropriate clinical context.
candidate.source_document_title: 2024 Guideline for the Management of Lower Extremity Peripheral Artery Disease; How Is PAD Diagnosed?
candidate.source_locator: 2024 PAD guideline — resting ABI for PAD detection; AHA How Is PAD Diagnosed? — normal ABI 1.0–1.4, ≤0.90 abnormal, >1.40 noncompressible
candidate.source_organization: American Heart Association / American College of Cardiology
candidate.stem: A client with suspected lower-extremity peripheral artery disease has a resting ankle-brachial index (ABI) of 0.82. How should the nurse interpret this result?
